title: NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own) — Premium Account Balances Set Against a Renewal Remittance
content:
**Setting a premium account balance against the renewal remittance (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own))**

*Credit balances.* For a credit balance no larger than the renewal premium on a policy whose insured is the payor of record and makes a renewal remittance before the term end, and only for such a balance, the balance is set against that remittance as the set-off rule states; every other credit, a credit balance larger than the renewal premium included, is refunded to the payor of record, and every refund is paid to the payor of record: payee lender escrow when the premium payor is the lender's escrow account, and payee insured otherwise.

*Balances owed.* For a renewal remittance the insured makes before the term end while the policy's premium account shows a balance owed, and only for such a remittance, the remittance also pays that balance as the set-off rule states; every other payment is accepted only by one of the accepted payment methods and is applied to the policy and term named on the payment; it is never moved to another policy of the same customer.

*The set-off rule* reads the policy's premium account — everything charged and every refund paid out, less every payment and every credit — and applies when the insured is the payor of record:

| Payor of record | Premium account | Effect on the remittance |
|---|---|---|
| The insured | Holds a credit balance (no larger than the renewal premium) | The balance is subtracted from the remittance |
| The insured | Holds a credit balance larger than the renewal premium | Not set off; the credit is refunded to the payor of record |
| The insured | Shows a balance owed | The balance owed is added to the remittance |
| The lender's escrow account, or a nil balance | — | Nothing is set against the remittance |

*Hypothetical cases.* With a renewal premium of 1,500.00 dollars: an insured-paid policy holding a 120.00-dollar credit remits 1,380.00; one owing 80.00 remits 1,580.00; one holding a 1,600.00-dollar credit has nothing set off and the credit is refunded.
